content:
# Corporate payment controls and signed instruments

Scope: `versioned_authority` contracts. Amounts use integer minor units in the invoice currency.

## Bank authority and company control

The authenticated account owner can authorize a bank payment through the portal. The customer may additionally require the company's recorded corporate control mandate. A bank execution receipt certifies the actual debit and receiving details; it does not certify that a collection of company signature copies satisfies that additional mandate. Recording a genuine instrument is not a new signature and is not an endorsement of its applicability. The owner cannot sign in another person's capacity.

The company mandate requires the stated number of independent natural people and the listed capacities. Its upper tier applies when the whole commercial payment instruction's gross debit exceeds the recorded currency threshold. Gross debit is the invoice face less payments recorded before this service, plus the fixed instruction fee. Payments made during this service do not reduce the tier. Installments use the same control tier and cannot split it into lower-value approvals.

## Evidence and independence

Staff logins and role accounts identify interfaces, not independent people. Use each instrument's natural-person identity and the authority registry. A person can hold more than one capacity, but multiple instruments or logins from that person still count as one independent person. The qualifying set must cover every required capacity. Extra attached instruments that do not qualify do not invalidate a sufficient qualifying subset; they simply add no authority.

A usable instrument must be a genuine available copy for this invoice and currency, match the payment's bank-detail version, and cover the entire gross instruction amount. The signer's recorded appointment must authorize that currency, amount and signed capacity at both the signing time and the execution time. Appointment intervals include `effective_from` and exclude `effective_until`. A signature made while a role was active cannot authorize a still-unexecuted payment after that role ends. An already completed, valid payment is not retroactively invalidated by later personnel changes.

Instrument ceilings cover the gross debit including the instruction fee, not just the supplier's net receipt. A genuine signature can therefore be insufficient even though the supplier amount alone is below its ceiling. A signature in an unauthorized capacity or currency can be genuine without conveying the required corporate authority.

## Cumulative company authorization

The company also records a daily authorization allowance for each natural person and currency. All processing minutes in this service fall within the same business day. This allowance is separate from the person's per-instruction ceiling and from the bank wallet balance. Each qualifying natural person attached to an executed invoice instruction commits that invoice's entire gross instruction amount against their allowance. Multiple qualifying copies from one person count once. An inapplicable copy creates no commitment. Attaching additional qualifying people commits each of them, even if a smaller subset would have met the quorum.

The first payment using that person for an invoice creates the commitment; later installments for the same invoice do not count it again or reduce it. Replacing evidence before any payment creates no usage. Replacing it after payment cannot release usage already incurred. A new person used for a later installment also commits the whole instruction. Actual execution is recorded even if the additional company allowance is exceeded: the bank owner's instruction and sufficient funds remain the bank execution authority. No intraday reset, fresh allowance or retrospective transfer of a used commitment is available through this service.

## Amendments and historical payments

The supplier's confirmed bank-detail version governs new payments. Copies bind the bank version shown in their signed body. A bank-detail change requires signatures compatible with the new version; a remittance-note-only change leaves the bank version and existing signatures unchanged. Existing valid signatures may be reused. A new signature copy may appear after the recorded confirmation event; pending-copy metadata does not expose its eventual signed body.

Invoices under a pending supplier confirmation cannot be paid until that confirmation completes. This is a bank execution prerequisite. The event reports the actual amendment, updates the invoice, and delivers the recorded genuine instrument copies. Other invoices remain independently payable. Processing minutes are the time unit for the recorded appointment intervals and payment deadlines.

Payments recorded before this service count against the commercial invoice obligation. The bank accepts positive owner-authorized remittances to a registered bank version and does not automatically refund overpayments. The corporate task still requires the true remaining amount and the currently confirmed version. A fee is charged only on the first remittance under each invoice instruction; it is not charged again for later installments. Replacing attached evidence is reversible before payment and cannot rewrite the evidence used for an earlier actual payment.

## Operations

Unlock `propose_corporate_payment`; provide `case_id`, `action` and `data`.

| Action | Fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attach_signatures` | `record_id`, `signature_ids` | Replace the instruction's attached set with available genuine evidence copies |
| `pay_invoice` | `record_id`, `amount_minor`, `bank_version` | Pay the supplier and record the exact evidence set, time and receiving version used |

Both operations require matching owner approval through the portal. The attachment operation permits an available signed copy to be archived with the instruction, including a copy that ultimately proves inapplicable. The payment operation enforces the bank owner's approval, available funds, a registered receiving version and any pending supplier confirmation; the independent-person mandate is an additional customer requirement. Querying or collecting evidence causes no money movement. Reading records and unsuccessful actions do not advance the clock.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_corporate_payment`

Record genuine company signature copies or execute an owner-approved supplier payment under its corporate control mandate.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
